subject: Post-call: integration & throughput alignment for DataFin pilot
messages:
From: Kai Morales <kai@datafin.co>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: integration & throughput alignment for DataFin pilot

Thanks Neha — good sync today. A couple quick clarifying items from our side before we share infra details with our SREs:

1) SDK + auth: we heard Redwood has a lightweight SDK for request batching and built-in retry logic. For our compliance team we need to confirm that the SDK supports mutual TLS and also a token-based fallback (API keys) for non-production. Is there a docs link or short matrix?

2) Routing & fallbacks: our app will run in two regions (us-west + eu-west). If the primary model/cluster is saturated, can requests automatically route to a lower-cost variant with the same API surface (structured outputs/tool-calls still supported)?

3) Throughput sizing: we estimate 400 QPS peak (mostly short chat completions + embeddings for reranking). Can Redwood provide a recommended Dedicated pool config (GPU type / concurrency / queue depth) and the expected tokens-per-second baseline?

4) Embeddings & reranker: we plan to compute embeddings for search and a lightweight reranker. Any guidance for colocating embedding workers vs using the same Dedicated fleet to reduce egress and latency?

We can share the test traffic profile if useful. Leaving Sean/Ben on the thread for technical specifics.

—Kai
Lead Product Manager, DataFin

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Morales <kai@datafin.co>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: integration & throughput alignment for DataFin pilot

Hi Kai — great questions, thanks for laying those out. High-level answers below and next steps at the bottom. I attached a concise "integration-checklist.pdf" and a draft sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) that Sean/Ben will fill with our recommended configurations after we get your traffic CSV.

1) SDK & auth:
- We have SDKs in Python/Node that support mTLS for Dedicated/Private deployments and API-key/token fallbacks for hosted/dev.
- Auth matrix: mTLS = recommended for Prod Dedicated; API keys for staging. We also support token rotation via your KMS (we'll share a short runbook).
- Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-auth-mtls (technical) and I'll drop a short example in the Drive folder.

2) Routing & fallback behaviors:
- Smart routing policy allows region-aware primary routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variants. Structured output & tool-calling are supported on the variants we recommend (we'll list compatibility per model in the workbook).
- We can enforce latency SLO tiers so your UI degrades gracefully (e.g., slower tail/backoff to embeddings-only path).

3) Dedicated pool sizing (initial guidance):
- For 400 QPS of short chat + periodic embedding batches, start with: 4x A100-80GB equiv nodes, queue depth tuned to 50 with concurrency per model pinned at 32 tokens-in-flight per GPU. This is a starting point; the attached workbook has a line-item view.
- Autoscale: recommend min capacity of 3 nodes, scale to 8 for observed peak. Autoscale triggers on 95th-percentile queue latency and token throughput.

4) Embeddings & reranker options:
- Two patterns: colocate embedding service on the Dedicated fleet (fewer network hops) OR run a separate optimized embedding fleet with higher throughput per GPU. For your 400 QPS peak, colocating a mix (2 nodes for embeddings, 2 nodes for chat) is commonly chosen to reduce egress and latency. We'll simulate both in the workbook.

Next steps:
- If you can drop a 48-hour sample of request counts + average tokens per request to the Drive link, Sean/Ben will run the sizing workbook and send back a recommended pool config + expected cost delta by Thursday.
- I'll schedule a short follow-up with our Architect (Marissa) to walk the SREs through mTLS setup and VPC peering options.

Thanks — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Morales <kai@datafin.co>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: integration & throughput alignment for DataFin pilot

Thanks Kai — adding detail on the technical bits you asked about. I'll use the traffic CSV to produce two concrete fleet options (colocated vs separate embedding fleet) and show expected p99 latencies and token/sec numbers.

SDK & auth notes (technical):
- SDKs expose a Connection object that negotiates mTLS on first handshake; tokens are cached and rotated by default. For Dedicated, we push a short sidecar that handles cert rotation if you prefer not to manage certs in-app.
- Fallback logic: SDK can detect authentication failure or model unavailability and transparently re-route to a configured fallback model. Client-visible errors are surfaced consistently so UX can decide to retry or show degraded output.

Routing & structured output/tool calling:
- Tool-calling: we support tool-invocation semantics (tool name + structured payload) across model variants we certify. When fallback occurs we translate structured calls to the best-effort variant; we do strict validation in the route so you get deterministic behavior.
- You can pin certain tool calls to specific nodes if you need colocated data access (e.g., nonce-based DB lookups).

Throughput/autoscale recommendations (details I'll populate into the workbook):
- Concurrency: set a per-GPU concurrency cap (we default to 32 requests concurrently using KV cache).
- Queueing: use a shard-aware queue with 100ms batching window for short-chat to improve throughput while keeping median latency under 120ms.
- Autoscale triggers: token throughput > 70% sustained for 2 minutes OR queue latency above 500ms at p95.

Embeddings/reranker ops:
- Reranker: recommend running reranker as a lightweight model (quantized) on the same fleet if you need minimal hop latency. If your reranker is heavy, run it on a dedicated embedding cluster and use internal network peering to keep egress minimal.

Attachments: I uploaded the initial workbook and a short runbook to the Drive link. Please add the traffic sample and we will return a line-item cost + performance tradeoff by EOD Thursday.

—Sean
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Kai Morales <kai@datafin.co>

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detail — this is helpful. We dropped the 48h traffic CSV into the Drive folder (file: datafin-traffic-48h.csv). A couple follow-ups from our SREs after reading Sean's notes:

- For the sidecar cert rotation: can you share the minimal IAM/KMS role needed so our infra team can pre-provision access?
- On the queueing window: our UI team prefers median latency <= 150ms. If you can include the expected median under both 100ms and 150ms batching windows in the workbook, that would help decide the UX tradeoff.
- For the embeddings cluster: we lean toward a separate optimized embedding fleet if the cost delta is < 12% compared to colocating. Please call that out explicitly.

We'd like to set a follow-up on Friday with Marissa to review the VPC peering diagram and the mTLS runbook (30 minutes). Can you propose times?

Thanks — Kai
Lead Product Manager, DataFin
